section.title: Common configurations for automated &hanasr;
section.para: Below is a summary of the most common and newly supported configurations for SAPHanaSR-angi. For the complete support matrix for all supported topologies, see .

tip.title: SAPHanaSR-angi configuration variants
tip.para: SAPHanaSR-angi introduces two configuration variants that allow administrators to choose the failover behavior that best aligns with their operational and availability requirements. While both variants provide &ha; for &hana;, they differ in how they respond to failures and balance recovery speed against service stability.

listitem.para: Progressive variant: Optimized for rapid recovery by proactively fencing the affected site when critical &hana; or file system failures are detected, enabling fast and reliable failover. This is the recommended option for most new deployments, particularly in cloud and performance-optimized environments.

Conservative variant: Prioritizes service stability by attempting to recover &hana; locally before fencing cluster nodes, reducing the likelihood of unnecessary fencing. This variant is best suited for traditional on-premises environments where maximizing local recovery is preferred over the fastest possible failover.

varlistentry.term: Scale-up, performance-optimized [A' => B], including read-enabled on the secondary site [A' => B"]

listitem.para: In the performance-optimized scenario, an &hana; RDBMS site A is synchronizing with an &hana; RDBMS site B on a second node. As the &hana; RDBMS on the second node is configured to preload the tables, the takeover time is typically very short.
Read access can be allowed on the secondary site. To support this read-enabled scenario, a second virtual IP address is added to the cluster and bound to the secondary role of the system replication.

&hana; XSA stand-alone is supported in the cluster by deploying XSA worker nodes alongside the &hana; master/worker nodes. Dedicated IP addresses are assigned to the primary XSA worker as well as the primary HANA master/worker node to ensure consistent service access. &hanasr; is enabled between the two HANA master/worker nodes, while a shared NFS file system maintains the XSA work directory across both sites to support seamless failover. The &sleha; solution for SAP XSA stand-alone is based on the &ha; architecture for &hana; scale-out ERP, with the SAPHanaSR-angi Progressive variant.

varlistentry.term: DR region with passive cluster (Technology Preview) {D <= C} <- [A' => B]

listitem.para: This deployment consists of a production region protected by a &ha; cluster using the SAPHanaSR-angi scale-up performance-optimized with Progressive variant. A separate disaster recovery (DR) region is equipped with a passive &ha; cluster to support recovery operations. In the event of a disaster, failover to the DR region is performed through a manual DR takeover process. There is no automated cluster takeover between the production and DR sites.
